references.text: The command to remember and keep all of God's commands is central in the Shema, where Israel is urged to love the Lord with all their heart.
The call to be holy because God is holy is a recurring theme in the Mosaic Law.
God commands Israel to be holy because He, the Lord their God, is holy.
Israel is urged to consecrate themselves and keep God's statutes, for it is the Lord who sanctifies them.
Israel is a holy people, chosen by the Lord among all peoples on earth.
God has declared Israel to be His own people, who must keep all His commands and be a holy nation.
Israel shall be a kingdom of priests and a holy nation if they keep God's covenant.
Peter quotes Leviticus and urges believers to be holy in all their conduct, because God is holy.
Believers are called a holy people, a people whom God has acquired to proclaim His mighty works.
God chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world, so that we should be holy and blameless before Him.
God did not call us to impurity, but to holiness.
